settings_backup_lead: A copy of awg-manager data: tunnels, WDTT/FreeTurn, sing-box configuration, routes and settings. Files built for this particular router (kernel modules, the sing-box binary), the sing-box cache, pid files and the run/ service directory are not included: on restore the existing ones are kept, and on a new router sing-box has to be reinstalled with the button. Related processes are briefly stopped before creating or restoring; after a restore a cold restart is performed with linked tunnel ports synchronized.

tunnels_awg_about_desc: A WireGuard fork with traffic obfuscation. Three protocol generations:
tunnels_awg_about_v1: Basic obfuscation: header modification (H1–H4), junk packets (Jc/Jmin/Jmax), message sizes (S1–S2).
tunnels_awg_about_v15: Protocol mimicry: initiation packets (I1–I5) disguise the connection as QUIC, DTLS, STUN, DNS.
tunnels_awg_about_v2: Header randomization: H1–H4 are set as ranges and generated on every handshake.
tunnels_awg_about_kernel_tail: — traffic is processed directly in the Linux kernel, which reduces CPU load.

awg_score_h_hp_detail: The header is encrypted by header protection — H1–H4 values are not visible on the wire, the default 1–4 is acceptable.
awg_score_h_default_detail: H1=1 H2=2 H3=3 H4=4 — the message type bytes of standard WireGuard; the handshake signature is visible to DPI.
awg_score_h_default_fix: Set unique H1–H4 (≥ 5) or ranges like 10000-20000 — values 1–4 are the WireGuard signature.
awg_score_h_below_five_detail: Values {values} overlap with WireGuard message types 1–4.
awg_score_h_below_five_fix: Raise the H values to ≥ 5 — 1–4 match WireGuard message types.
awg_score_h_narrow_detail: An H range is narrower than 1000 values — low header entropy.
awg_score_h_narrow_fix: Widen H ranges to at least 1000 values.
awg_score_jc_hp_detail: With header protection the handshake size does not reveal the protocol — junk packets are optional.
awg_score_jc_zero_detail: No junk packets — the handshake can be detected by size.
awg_score_jc_zero_fix: Set Jc in the 3–10 range with Jmin/Jmax — junk packets mask the handshake size.
awg_score_jc_high_detail: Jc={jc} — extra traffic on every handshake with no gain in resistance.
awg_score_jrange_hp_detail: With header protection junk packet sizes do not reveal the protocol.
awg_score_jrange_narrow_detail: The junk packet size spread is under 30 bytes — the size is predictable.
awg_score_jrange_narrow_fix: Widen Jmin/Jmax so the difference is ≥ 30 bytes.
awg_score_s_hp_detail: The first 12 bytes of padding carry the header protection nonce.
awg_score_s_wg_detail: Handshake padding is an AmneziaWG parameter; plain WireGuard has none.
awg_score_s_zero_detail: {title}=0 — the {kind} packet size matches standard WireGuard.
awg_score_s_zero_fix: Set {title} > 0 — otherwise the handshake size matches WireGuard.
awg_score_s_ok_detail: The handshake packet size is changed.
awg_score_s56_detail: Amnezia rule: S1 + 56 must not equal S2, otherwise the Init and Response sizes are linked.
awg_score_s56_fix: Change S1 or S2 so that S1 + 56 ≠ S2.
awg_score_s31_fix: For AWG 3.1 set S1 = S2 = S3 = S4 ≥ 12 (Amnezia recommendation).
awg_score_i1_ok_detail: The <b>/<r> tags are valid, the first packet imitates {cps}.
awg_score_i1_unset_detail: First-packet mimicry is not used. Optional: I1 with QUIC/TLS/DNS.
